news_synthesis: The recent headlines (last 28 days) are largely match previews and squad news for Real Madrid’s La Liga fixtures against Elche and Rayo Vallecano, plus a report on José Mourinho’s preferred defensive setup for the Atlético derby. One headline references a Liverpool player’s performance against Fulham, which is not relevant to Alexander-Arnold’s current situation at Real Madrid. No recent news directly addresses Alexander-Arnold’s form, role, or performance in the last 28 days.
fit_read: The available stats offer a mixed and incomplete picture for a vertical, fast-transition, high-line, counter-pressing system. On the positive side, 22 crosses and 6 key passes in only 214 minutes suggest a progressive, chance-creating profile that could suit quick vertical play, and 7 interceptions indicate some reading of the game in defensive phases. However, only 1 tackle won and 0 fouls committed across 4 matches provide very little evidence of the aggressive, ball-winning intensity that a counter-press demands — though the low sample size (2 starts, 214 minutes) makes this hard to weigh heavily. The stats listed do not include pace, sprint distance, or high-intensity running data, so the speed-dependent aspects of transition fit cannot be assessed at all. Similarly, no data on pressures, duels, or recovery runs is available, so the pressing and high-line suitability remains largely unjudged. Given the small sample and missing key metrics, a neutral score of 3 is appropriate rather than a confident extreme. If the scout’s role notes are present, they should be treated as the scout’s own observation, not verified fact, and weighed alongside these limited signals.

findings: The 6 key passes come from Understat over 206 minutes, not 214, and the paragraph conflates the two minute totals when attributing both stats to the same 214-minute sample. (in: "22 crosses and 6 key passes in only 214 minutes suggest a progressive, chance-creating profile that could suit quick vertical play")

Interceptions alone do not fairly support a claim about 'reading of the game'; this is an interpretive overreach from a single counting stat. (in: "7 interceptions indicate some reading of the game in defensive phases")

Zero fouls committed is framed as evidence of low intensity, but low fouls could equally reflect disciplined positioning; the stat does not fairly support the intensity inference. (in: "only 1 tackle won and 0 fouls committed across 4 matches provide very little evidence of the aggressive, ball-winning intensity that a counter-press demands")
No scoring scale or rubric is present in the available data, so asserting a specific numeric score is unsupported. (in: "a neutral score of 3 is appropriate")
